subject: Dedicated capacity: GPU family & concurrency workplan
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Ari Cohen <ari@quantify.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity: GPU family & concurrency workplan

Ari — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and the asks we committed to: 

1) Goal and deployment mode check
- You confirmed the primary goal is low-latency inference for customer-facing similarity search + chat features.
- You are evaluating Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool) but want to understand when Hosted API is sufficient vs when Private VPC is needed for data controls.

2) Sizing inputs we need from your side (short version)
- Target sustained TPS and peak TPS (per model).
- Typical prompt/response token mix: average tokens in request / average tokens in response; 95th pct lengths if available.
- Concurrency expectations (number of concurrent users or concurrent requests at peak).
- Any P95 latency SLO targets (e.g., 200ms/500ms).

3) Our immediate proposal items
- We will run a short sizing matrix for A100 80GB, H100 80GB, and 80GB 8-bit quantized variants, plus a mixed pool recommendation.
- Guidance on batching/concurrency tradeoffs and a recommended starting autoscaling policy for Dedicated.
- A short cost delta comparison to Hosted for the first 3 months of expected traffic.

Action items: 
- Ari to share a coarse token profile CSV (sample rows OK) and peak/sustained TPS targets — by EOD Tuesday.
- Ben/Me to produce a 1-page Dedicated sizing plan and two configuration options: conservative (lower GPU count, higher latency SLO) and performance (more GPUs, tighter latency).

Attachments: I attached a template token-profile CSV and a sketch of the initial POC topology.

If the above looks right I’ll kick off the sizing calc tomorrow and loop in Priyom for ops/quantization notes.

Thanks,
Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: GPU family & concurrency workplan

Thanks Karthik — good recap. Sending the rough numbers below and attaching a trimmed sample token profile. Hope this helps.

Quick answers: 
- Sustained TPS (avg): 45 requests/sec across our primary ranking model during business hours.
- Peak TPS: 160 rps sustained for ~10-15 minute bursts during product updates.
- Token mix (sample averages): request 180 tokens, response 300 tokens; 95th pct response ~1,200 tokens for long context cases.
- Concurrency: we expect ~75 concurrent sessions generating requests during peak.
- Latency SLO: 500ms P95 for the ranking model; 800ms P95 is acceptable for long chat responses.

We are currently model-tenanting a 7b and a 13b open model (both LLAMA-derived). Happy to test quantized variants but we need to keep quality regression <2% on our eval set.

Attached: sample_token_profile_trim.csv

Also: we will likely need a VPC deployment for customer data in late Q3 — initially the Dedicated pool can be in Redwood-hosted with strict retention and KMS controls.

—Ari
Ari Cohen
Head of ML Infrastructure, Quantify.ai

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Ari Cohen <ari@quantify.ai>
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 16:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: GPU family & concurrency workplan

Karthik/Ari — looping in Priyom for ops/quantization input. A few notes from our side after quick back-of-envelope with Ari’s numbers: 

- Baseline recommendation (start): 4x H100-80GB for the ranking model pool, with a secondary mixed-type pool of 2x A100-80GB to handle long-context chat workloads. Rationale: H100 gives better throughput for transformer attention and larger KV cache headroom; A100 has slightly better price/perf for long-context quantized runs.
- If we can accept 8-bit quantization (we’ll validate via eval), we can reduce memory pressure and fit more concurrency per GPU — likely a 30–40% cost delta. Priyom: can you confirm whether Redwood’s mixed-precision path + our 8-bit kernels can meet Quantify’s <2% eval regression bar?
- Autoscale policy idea: keep a min pool of 2 GPUs (warm), scale up in discrete steps at 60 rps and 120 rps thresholds, scale down after 10m of sustained lower traffic. This keeps tail latency predictable.

Karthik — two asks: 
1) Ari, can you confirm which model (7b vs 13b) is the dominant traffic generator for the ranking path? We used aggregated numbers above but we should size per-model.
2) Priyom, can you prepare a quick test plan we can run during the POC (1) quantization A/B, (2) concurrency sweep, (3) cold vs warm KV cache measurement).

I’ll draft the 1-pager and numbers tomorrow, Karthik — want me to include cost proformas for both Dedicated and Hosted delta for the first 90 days?

Ben
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: Ari Cohen <ari@quantify.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: GPU family & concurrency workplan

Thanks Ben — quick answers inline and confirming next steps.

- Dominant model for ranking: 7b handles ~70% of ranking traffic; 13b is used for long-response chat and rare analytic workloads.
- We’re okay with an initial 8-bit quantization test as long as we gate it behind the eval suite and keep a rollback path.
- Confirmed: we want the Dedicated pool initially hosted by Redwood with KMS-managed keys. We’ll plan for a VPC cutover in Q3; can you include an estimated cutover checklist in the sizing doc (networking, KMS rotation, cert exchange)?

Next steps: 
- I’ll drop the detailed token CSV in the shared Drive link (will email the link to ops later today).
- Priyom/Prioritized test plan: please share a brief (<1 page) test matrix and target pass metrics.
- Ben/Karthik: please share the 1-pager with the two capacity options and the cost delta by EOD Thursday.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — looking forward to the sizing doc.

—Ari
